summary: Caverna is a big, generous worker-placement farming game where you build up a dwarf family, cave, and land while juggling multiple viable strategies (farming, mining, weapons for expeditions) with almost no direct conflict. It has a gentler, more forgiving feel than Agricola since you're never fully locked out of feeding your family or forced into begging cards.
praised: Huge variety of viable strategies and near-total freedom from a hand of restrictive cards
Satisfying sense of building up a personal empire/engine
Tactile, chunky components and a beautiful, functional player board
Less punishing and more solo-friendly than Agricola
criticised: Long playtime and significant downtime with full player counts
Analysis paralysis from the sheer number of options each turn
Very heavy table presence and setup/teardown time
Weapons/expedition subsystem feels like a mini-game bolted onto the farming core
Can feel like a solitaire multiplayer game with little direct interaction

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking, mostly parallel empire-building

scoring.why: Points come from a wide scoring table covering rooms, fields, animals, resources, and family size, so the winner is whoever builds the most efficient, well-rounded farm rather than one who maximizes a single category
